title: How findings relate to a claim (support / undermine / question)
subtitle: Words in Context · 8 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **8 of the official questions in Words in Context are this one** — 4 Easy, 2 Medium, 2 Hard.
It is bottom-heavy, which makes it cheap points. Secure it early.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- The text sets up a belief, hypothesis or skepticism, then brings in researchers, data or a study, and the blank is the verb or noun that links the new evidence to the earlier view.
- The choices are verbs of reasoning or attitude, such as assume, question, confirm, reveal, anticipate or regret.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Decide whether the new evidence agrees with the earlier view or goes against it.
- 2) Decide whether the blank describes the evidence or the people who held the view.
- 3) Pick the choice with that exact relationship, for example confirming rather than merely showing.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You choose a neutral 'research-sounding' verb such as reveal or inspect that doesn't express agreement or disagreement.
Or you mix up who is doing what, for example you pick 'questioned' for people who actually held the assumption.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
